key_insight: A classically emulated quantum circuit can match or outperform a comparable CNN only in some data regimes, but it is not universally superior.
engineering_relevance: For medical image classification, hybrid quantum-inspired components may be useful as drop-in architectural alternatives, especially when training data are moderate and explainability matters.
method: Compared a hybrid quantum-inspired CNN (HQiCNN) against a parameter-matched classical CNN with one intermediate dense layer replaced.
Evaluated both models on two real medical image datasets while systematically varying hyperparameters for a fair comparison.
Added SHAP-based explainability metrics (|SHAP| IoU and EMD_pos) to compare what each model attends to.
evidence_signal: Across two datasets and multiple hyperparameter settings, HQiCNN performed best in intermediate-data regimes, while the classical CNN won on the largest training sets; removing entanglement kept performance similar and improved simulation scalability.
watch_item: Quantum-emulated layers may be computationally expensive and their benefits depend strongly on dataset size, so gains may not persist at scale.
paper_title: Do emulated quantum circuits change what CNNs look at? Performance and explainability comparison in medical image classification
